cohort: The study included 204,723 women aged 15-49 years who had a pregnancy in the past 5 years preceding the survey, selected from the National Family Health Survey 5 (NFHS-5) data.
finding: The use of unclean cooking fuels was significantly associated with an increased risk of stillbirth (OR = 1.34, 95 % CI: 1.13-1.58, p < 0.001) compared to clean fuels.
mod_finding: Undergoing caesarean delivery was identified as a factor associated with a higher stillbirth risk.
cross-section timing: Data from 2019 to 2021, covering pregnancies in the past 5 years preceding the survey.
